sentences.text:
Shri R.K. Sharma, learned senior counsel with Shri V.K.
Agrawal, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri R.K. Soni, learned Government Advocate for the respondents/State.

1. Present petition seeks review of common order dated 09.12.2019 passed inter alia in W.P.
No.21937/2019 by this Court declining exercise of power of judicial review thereby upholding the order of preventive detention dated 23.09.2019 passed by the District Magistrate, Bhind under the National Security Act, 1980.
2.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard on the question of admission.

3. Learned senior counsel for petitioner by referring to the decisions of this Court in Vishnu Prasad Shukla Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors., 1989 MPLJ 546, order dated 04.02.2019 passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P. No.25986/2018 (Annexure A/2) and order dated 08.11.2019 of another co-ordinate Bench of this Court rendered in W.P. No21768/2019 (Annexure A/3) submits that the order under review suffers from error apparent on the face of record for the following reasons:-
(a) Despite the undisputed fact of Advisory Board being not available from 04.06.2019 to 13.11.2019, this Court ought to have set aside the order of preventive detention owing to violation of safeguard in Art.22(4) of Constitution.
(b) District Magistrate was oblivious of the fact of petitioner being already in custody on the date of passing of order of preventive detention and therefore, impugned order ought to have been set aside on this short ground in view of decision of Apex Court in Huidrom Konungjao Singh Vs. State of Manipur, AIR 2012 SC 2002.

1 (c) Report of chemical analyst not having revealed the samples of food articles being dangerous for human consumption, no presumption could have been drawn by the District Magistrate of slow poison being spread in the society by manufacturing and selling artificial milk.
4. Taking up the second ground first, it is seen that the express reasons supplied to the petitioner justifying the order of preventive detention clearly reveal that District Magistrate was well aware of the fact that petitioner was arrested on 09.09.2019 in connection with offences punishable u/Ss.420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC r/w 51 and 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 registered as Crime No.12/2019.

sentences.text: Thus, the factum of petitioner being in custody at the time when order of preventive detention was passed was well within the knowledge of the District Magistrate and therefore, the aforesaid ground No.2 raised by learned counsel for petitioner has no force.

4.1 As regards the third ground, the order under review clearly reveals that factum of public analyst report disclosing samples to be adulterated and below standard but not harmful for human consumption was very much taken into account vide para 17 of the order under review.
Yet this Court consciously passed the order under review and therefore the said decision may be erroneous but not palpably erroneous.
4.2 Coming to the first ground of non-availability of Advisory Board, it is seen from the order under review that in para 18, this Court was mindful of this fact.

The Division Bench judgment in case of Vishnu Prasad Shukla (supra) of this Court does not assist the petitioner since the same was never raised as one of the grounds in the writ petition, neither was it pressed in the oral arguments submitted by learned counsel for petitioner.
Thus, it is obvious that this ground did not receive serious consideration by this Court while passing the order under review.
As such the judgment of Division Bench of this court in Vishnu Prasad's case is of no avail to petitioner.

5. Before parting it would be appropriate to mention that looking to the enormity of the damage to a very large section of society including small children as a direct result of the acts of petitioner in manufacturing synthetic milk and selling the same in the market camouflaged as real milk, the decision under review may have ignored a few technical glitches in the process of passing the order of preventive detention by the District Magistrate, keeping in mind the continued widespread damage caused to the community at large if the petitioner was allowed to enjoy liberty.
6. In view of above and in the absence of palpable error visible on record, this Court declines interference.
7. Accordingly, present review petition stands dismissed sans cost.

(Sheel Nagu) (Rajeev Kumar Shrivastava)
